thread:
maya: Heads-up — since ~03:15 UTC we've been seeing short-lived pod connections drop in the east-asia GPU pool. Spike in failures correlates with a large increase in NAT/conntrack entries on a subset of nodes. Not all nodes, looks concentrated on the RDMA-enabled AB zones. :grimacing:

liam: How widespread? is this impacting Dedicated nodes or just shared GPU pools? Any obvious dmesg / conntrack logs?

maya: Shared GPU pool so far, but a couple of internal customers reported transient RPC failures. Quick dumps: 
```
# ssh node-gpu-12
$ sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
262314
$ sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 262144
$ dmesg | tail -n 20
[...]
nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```
Also saw repeated TCP ephemeral ports exhaustion in kube-proxy logs and ib0 shows MTU 9000 while overlay iface is 1500.

arjun: That MTU mismatch + RDMA path + kernel bump last night smells like a fragmentation/GSO failure causing tons of tiny connections and conntrack churn. Which kernel was rolled?

maya: Kernel rolled to 5.15.0-82 last night via automated node image update; patch notes referenced RDMA driver update. We didn't have a forced cordon.

ops-bot: ALERT INC-2026-224: conntrack_saturation east-asia-gpupool — 300+ dropped pod connections in 5m. Pager duty: oncall-eric. https://redwood.ops/incident/INC-2026-224 :rotating_light:

liam: Immediate mitigation options: (1) increase net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max and shorten established TCP timeout, (2) roll nodes back to previous kernel, (3) cordon-only heavy SNAT nodes and route traffic to spare capacity. Which is least disruptive?

arjun: Short-term I can push sysctl changes via daemonset: 
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600
```
That buys headroom. Also reduce kube-proxy conntrack settings (kube-proxy flags: --conntrack-max-per-core / --conntrack-min) and enable conntrack hashsize tuning. Long-term we need to fix MTU/GSO: set overlay MTU to 9000 or ensure offloads are consistent.

sarah: For quickest rollback, I can hold the node-image update and coordinate a rolling reboot back to 5.15.0-79 for the RDMA nodes. That would be slightly disruptive but reduces the immediate source. Which do we prefer?

juan: Confirmed: ib0 shows RX/TX fragmentation errors on 3 nodes. Geneve overlay was still at 1500 MTU (CNI config). Putting the overlay->9000 is non-trivial for live pods (need drain/cordon). Suggest: 1) apply conntrack headroom (arjun), 2) cordon the top 10% offending nodes and drain to spares, 3) schedule MTU change + drained rolling update overnight.

maya: Plan then: arjun apply conntrack sysctl now (T+5m), liam to adjust kube-proxy conntrack flags via patch to daemonset (T+20m), sarah to prepare kernel rollback playbook if headroom doesn't reduce errors (T+30m), juan to prepare node list for cordon/drain and MTU migration (T+30m). I'll notify affected customers and set incident status.

ops-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-224 declared — runbook attached: https://redwood.ops/runbooks/conntrack-saturation. Ops lead: maya. Priority: P2.

liam: Added an internal dashboard panel for conntrack table usage per-node and SNAT allocation so we can watch the effect of the sysctl. Sharing shortly.

maya: Thanks — keep updates here. If anyone sees persistent nf_conntrack: table full in dmesg after the sysctl + kube-proxy patch, escalate and we'll start kernel rollback. :thumbsup:
